midia-today.why: One ordered list of what needs you today, each item with why it matters, its impact and the next step.
steps: Open [[MI DÍA]]. Read the first card: who, why, what changed and the impact.
Click the card's main button to go straight to the record.
Or act from the card: note what happened with [[Registrar]], postpone with [[Mañana]] / [[En 3 días]] / [[1 semana]], or save a customer's promise with [[Guardar promesa]].
When you finish something, click [[✓ Hecho]] and set what comes next without leaving My Day.
midia-today.expect: The number next to MY DAY in the menu matches the list. A card you already handled disappears or moves down.

midia-agenda.why: Reserve time for the work that matters today and tomorrow.
steps: On a card, click [[Primer espacio libre de hoy]], or pick a time and click [[Agendar a esta hora]].
In Your agenda, use [[Mover]] to change a block's time, or mark it done or remove it.
midia-agenda.expect: The block shows in Your agenda at the right time and does not overlap another one.

miplan.t: My Plan and the file for Outlook
miplan.why: Your week of planned work, and a file to take it to Outlook.
steps: Open the [[Mi Plan]] tab. Under “Worth reserving” are the work blocks SOLU proposes for your week.
Click the button that starts with [[Reservar los]] (it says how many blocks there are) to put them in your agenda.
To see them in Outlook: if your calendar is already connected, click [[Enviar a mi Outlook]]. If not, click [[Descargar .ics]] and open the file: Outlook offers to add the events.
To connect it once and for all, click [[Conectar Outlook]].
miplan.expect: The events in Outlook match the blocks of My Plan. “Send to my Outlook” only shows once your calendar is connected; until then you see “Connect Outlook”.

tasks.why: Small tasks that do not belong to a Need's card.
steps: Type the task, pick the date and click [[Agregar]].
Change the estimated minutes if needed.
Click [[Eliminar]] to remove one.
tasks.expect: The task shows in the list. Deleting asks for confirmation first.

comunicacion.why: Keep customers' WhatsApp messages, calls and emails in one place. SOLU separates what the customer said (fact) from what SOLU deduces (inference).
steps: Paste a WhatsApp message or a call summary and click [[Guardar y que SOLU lo lea]].
Check the "SOLU understood" panel: facts and inferences are marked. Click [[Guardar]] to keep an item or [[Descartar]] if it does not apply.
Link the conversation to a Need with [[Vincular]] (or choose "New Need").

To have AI build the Need from the whole email or message, click [[Crear Necesidad con IA]]: “New Need” opens with the conversation already in place. Click [[Armar la Necesidad]], review and create the Need; the conversation stays linked to it.
Answer with [[Enviar desde el correo de la empresa]], or close it with [[Nada más que hacer aquí]].
comunicacion.expect: Urgent or unanswered conversations also show in My Day. Emails go out from sales@indsolusa.com. “Fetch customer emails” brings the emails that reached the company mailbox in the last 14 days, only from people or companies already registered as customers. “Create Need with AI” appears when the AI key is connected and the conversation has no Need yet.

buzon-necesidad.t: Mailbox emails: create a Need from an email you sent or received
buzon-necesidad.why: Take an email that is already in your mailbox or the company's, sent or received, and let AI build the Need from its text, with no copying and pasting.
steps: Open [[MI DÍA]], the [[Comunicación]] tab and click [[Correos del buzón]].
Under “1 · WHICH MAILBOX” choose [[Mi buzón]] or [[Buzón de la empresa]], and [[Enviados]] or [[Recibidos]].
Under “2 · PICK THE EMAIL”, find the email and click [[Crear Necesidad con IA]] on its row.
“New Need” opens with the text of the email. Add what you know about the case and click [[Armar la Necesidad]].

Review what SOLU understood and click [[Pasar al formulario]]. If the customer was not on the list, check the new customer and contact data SOLU took from the email; check every box and create the Need.
buzon-necesidad.expect: You see the 30 most recent emails of the folder. This only reads: no email is moved, marked or stored. “My mailbox” is the email you log in to SOLU with; nobody opens another person's mailbox. If Microsoft does not find the mailbox, the page says so: SOLU only reads mailboxes of the same Microsoft 365 account as the company email. If Management also connected a mailbox that is not Microsoft's, its owner sees a third button with that address; only that person sees and opens it.

email.why: Send emails from sales@indsolusa.com with the company templates, in Spanish or English, without leaving SOLU.
steps: Open the [[Correo]] tab.
Pick a template (supplier quote request, follow-up, negotiation, delivery, offer or collection) and the language.
Pick the contact, check the text and send. If the tone sounds harsh, SOLU warns you but does not block you.
email.expect: The email arrives from sales@indsolusa.com. Try it first with your own address. The domain check (SPF, DKIM and DMARC) should look in order. On every template email you can type several recipients under “To”, and copies under “CC” and “BCC”, separated by commas. The email that sends a quote has the quote's PDF ticked as an attachment (it can be unticked). The “Progress on your request” and “Customer offer” emails have a “DRAFT WITH AI” block: when AI is connected, it writes a personalised draft from the Need's data, never naming the supplier or mentioning costs, and you review it before sending. Whoever has their own mailbox connected also sees the “Send from” list: they can send from the company email or from their mailbox. From their mailbox, the customer's reply arrives in their own email and SOLU does not match it by itself under “Replies”.

respuestas.why: Replies to the requests we send from SOLU are matched with their request automatically. Nobody has to look for them in the mailbox.
steps: Send a quote request from Find parts (see Market).
Open [[Respuestas]] and find the request: each supplier shows whether they replied and when.
Open a reply and take the price and lead time to the Need's source.
respuestas.expect: Automatic replies (out of office) and bounces are shown apart. SOLU checks the mailbox every 15 minutes.

explorar.why: Organise what we know about a market or a company: signals, open questions, plants and future needs.
steps: Open [[Mercados y empresas]] and go into «Mercado lácteo colombiano» (sample).
Review the signals and open questions of each company and plant.
When a real need appears, pass it to Commercial: a Need opens with all the context.
Set a next move: a dated task is created.
explorar.expect: A signal alone does not create a sales opportunity. Only a real need passes to Commercial.

prospectos.why: Find people SOLU does not know yet, by job title and company, in Apollo's database. Searching is free; revealing a person uses 1 Apollo credit.
steps: Open [[Explorar prospectos]]. If it says Apollo is not connected yet, Management follows the five steps shown there.
Type the job titles separated by commas (in Spanish and in English), where the person lives or the company's headquarters, and click [[Buscar en Apollo]].
Read the results: first name, partial last name, title, company and whether Apollo has their email.
On the person worth it, click [[Revelar · 1 crédito]] and confirm. They are added to “REVEALED PROSPECTS” with full name, work email and LinkedIn.
To work with them in SOLU, click [[Pasar a Clientes y Contactos]]: the customer is created if it did not exist and the person becomes a contact.
If they are no use, [[Descartar]].

If you already found the person elsewhere (Apollo's site, LinkedIn, a business card): under “REVEAL SOMEONE YOU ALREADY FOUND” paste the link to their LinkedIn profile, or type first name, last name and company, and click [[Pedir sus datos · 1 crédito]].
Management or Direction: [[Probar qué permite la cuenta]] says, without spending credits, whether the Apollo account allows searching and revealing from SOLU.
prospectos.expect: With Apollo's free plan, searching from SOLU may be blocked: the screen says so in Apollo's words, and you work by pasting the LinkedIn link. At the top you see the credits used this month and the cap. Revealing the same person twice does not spend another credit. If the company or the person was already in SOLU, they are linked without duplicating. Each prospect says who revealed it, when and with which search. SOLU never asks for personal emails or phone numbers.

economia.why: Explorer of the companies reported to Supersociedades: sales, growth and signals by sector and size.
steps: Open [[Economía]].
Filter by sector or size.
Open a company and compare it with another.
economia.expect: The data comes from the last Supersociedades upload made in “Load market data”.

fuentes.why: Upload data files (Excel or CSV) and review them before saving.
steps: Open [[Cargar datos del mercado]] and choose the file.
Review the preview: new rows, changes and errors.
Confirm the upload.
fuentes.expect: Nothing is saved without the review. People without one of those roles do not see this tab.

accounts.why: Everything about a customer: open Needs, history, how they pay and what equipment they have.
steps: Open "New customer". Under "Customer documents" choose the RUT (PDF downloaded from the DIAN) and, if you want, the Chamber of Commerce certificate.

SOLU fills in legal name, tax ID with its check digit (DV box, optional), state, city, address, phone and invoice email, marked "from RUT" or "from Chamber". Check them (if the check digit does not match, it says so). Only the legal name is required: choose the country (it changes the phone code), type the website as you know it and, if you want, the contact for promotions with the permission box. Click [[Crear cliente]].

Click anywhere on the customer's row to open their 360 view (the column "Invoiced · 12 months" says how much we invoiced them in the last year). Under "Documents" you can open the RUT, see what SOLU read or upload more files with [[Subir]].
Review the history, the billing pattern and the installed equipment.
Start a new need from here with [[Crear y abrir]]. A Need opens.
Billing profile: say whether they accept partial invoices and who receives the invoices, and [[Guardar]].
accounts.expect: If a customer with that tax ID already exists, SOLU does not create another and takes you to the existing one. Scanned or photographed RUTs are stored, but the boxes are filled in by hand. Charts only show with at least 3 data points.

estadisticas-cliente.why: How each customer has performed for us, month by month and compared with before: how much they ask for, how much they buy and pay, how long each step takes, how many emails they send us and how their credit limit has changed.
steps: Open the customer from the list. Above "ACTIVE NEEDS" is "STATISTICS · LAST 12 MONTHS" with six figures compared with the 12 months before. Click a figure or [[Ver todas las estadísticas mes a mes]].
Choose the period: [[Últimos 12 meses]], [[Últimos 24 meses]], [[Últimos 36 meses]] or [[Toda la historia]]. Each period is compared with the previous one of the same length.
Read each figure: its name says how it is counted. On the right, one bar per month; the grey line is the same month a year earlier.
Click a month (on a chart or in the table header): "What happened in …" appears at the top with each record behind that month's figures, and each one opens. Close it with [[Cerrar]].
Under "CREDIT LIMIT AND CLAIMS" open "Credit limit history" to see each change: date, before, after and who made it.
At the end, the table "Month by month, every figure" puts everything together, most recent month on the left.
estadisticas-cliente.expect: The figures come on their own from what is already recorded; there is nothing to fill in. Only money reconciled by Treasury and emails that reached the mailbox connected to SOLU count. Times are averages of that month's cases ("—" if there were none). A green arrow says the figure moved the good way and a red one the bad way; emails and the credit limit have no colour because going up or down is neither good nor bad by itself.

steps: Open "New contact". Choose the customer first; then first name, last name, title, email and, if you have it, the phone with its country code. Tick the permission box only if the person agreed to receive promotions. Click [[Crear contacto]].
Use [[Buscar]] to find someone.
contacts.expect: The contact shows in the customer's 360 and in the Need's contact list. Deleting asks for confirmation.

relacion.why: What matters to treat each person well: notes, open commitments and messages prepared with care.
steps: Open the file of Jorge Pérez (sample).
Add a note or a dated commitment.
Prepare a message: SOLU suggests a kind and direct tone.
relacion.expect: Each note shows who wrote it and when.

suppliers.why: How each supplier really delivers: real lead times, what was quoted versus what was bought.
steps: Create a supplier: open “New supplier”, type the name (the only required field) and click [[Crear proveedor]]. SOLU confirms “Supplier created” and leaves it in the list.
From a Need there is no need to come all the way here: on its Execute tab, [[+ Crear proveedor nuevo]] opens this form and, on saving, you return to the Need with the supplier already picked.
Open a supplier: review the real times to dispatch and what was quoted versus what was bought.
Start a need for one of their products with [[Crear y abrir]].
suppliers.expect: Facts only; there are no supplier scores.

localizar.why: Find who has a part by code, alias, brand or description, in Spanish or English, or by reading the text in a photo of a nameplate.
steps: Open [[Localizar repuestos]], type a code or a description, for example «1FK7» or «rodamiento 23148», and click [[Buscar]].
Or click [[Leer placa desde foto]]: SOLU reads the text on the nameplate and searches with it.
Open a result. Under “SUPPLIER OFFERS” is each supplier's evidence: saved offers, real lead times and earlier replies.
To save a supplier's offer, go back to the list, click [[Registrar cotización o proforma de proveedor]], upload their PDF and check what SOLU read before saving.
localizar.expect: Reading the text of a photo is free and works. Photo search with AI is off until the company connects the AI service.

localizar-internet.t: Search the internet for a part
localizar-internet.why: Find who sells today a piece that is not in our catalog or with our suppliers: SOLU searches the internet, checks the part number on each page and hands back the sellers by confidence level, with direct link and contact.
steps: Open [[Localizar repuestos]], type the piece's part number, name or brand and click [[Buscar]].

Go down to “SEARCH THE INTERNET” and open [[Responder unas preguntas y buscar]]. No question is required: brand, quantity, delivery country, whether used is acceptable, whether an equivalent is acceptable and which Need it is for. If that piece was already searched, you will see “Already searched” with the link to the result.
Click [[Buscar en internet]]. It takes 1 to 3 minutes; you can leave the page open or go and come back later.

Read “WHAT SOLU UNDERSTOOD” and then the sellers, from “HIGH CONFIDENCE” to “LOW CONFIDENCE”. Each one says why it has that confidence and brings “Direct link” and “Contact”: email, phone or contact form.
On the seller that suits you, pick the Need under “Save on the Need” and click [[Guardar opción]]. If you have already decided to go ahead with them, click [[Guardar y usar como fuente]].

To ask a seller for a price, click [[Escribirle al vendedor]]: the email “Price request to a seller” opens, already written with the piece, the quantity and the link where we saw it. Check “To”, the subject and the text, tick the photos you want attached and click [[Enviar correo]].
If SOLU left “QUESTIONS THAT WOULD SHARPEN THE SEARCH”, answer the ones you know and click [[Buscar otra vez con estas respuestas]].
localizar-internet.expect: High confidence: the exact part number was seen on the seller's page. Medium: everything suggests they have it, but it still has to be checked on the page. Low: worth asking them; the piece was not seen listed. Confidence does not rate the seller or the price. What a page shows is a reference, not an offer. “Save and use as source” puts the seller on file as a supplier and writes the source on the Need; you type the cost once the seller confirms it. Each search uses the AI (a few US cents) and is kept for the whole team. The email to the seller goes out from the company address with the request-for-quotation template, never names the customer and has the same options as the customer emails: several recipients, CC and BCC, “Rewrite with AI”, signature, attachments and “Keep internal only, don't send”. Once sent, the seller is marked “Email sent” and their reply arrives under MY DAY → Replies. If their email was not seen, the text comes ready to copy into their contact form. If a seller is missing the email or the phone, open “Find or type the contact” on their card: “Search the seller's site” reads their contact page and home page, and “Save contact” keeps what you type yourself.

rfq.t: Ask several suppliers for a quote
rfq.why: One request to several suppliers from sales@, instead of one email per supplier.
steps: Open [[Localizar repuestos]], search for the part and open it.
On the part, open [[Pedir precio a proveedor]] and click [[Enviar correo a uno o varios proveedores]].
Review the four blocks: “WHAT WE ASK FOR”, “To whom” (tick the suppliers), “WHAT WE ASK” and “DETAILS”.
Click [[Enviar solicitud]]. Follow the replies in MY DAY → Replies.
rfq.expect: One email per supplier goes out from sales@. The request is recorded and the replies arrive in Replies by themselves. If you will ask by phone or WhatsApp, use “Just create a to-do” instead of the email.

productos.why: What we know about a product, by code: aliases, packing, compatible parts and specifications, with the source of each fact.
steps: Open [[Productos]] and click a code.
Add a fact (alias, packing, compatibility or specification) with its source, and [[Guardar]].
Start a need for this product with [[Crear y abrir]].
productos.expect: Each fact shows who recorded it and its source.

journeys-board.t: New Need and the Needs board
journeys-board.why: Every order starts here: what the customer asks for is recorded, we confirm by email that we received it, and the date of the next contact is set. Below, the board shows every open Need by stage.
steps: At the top, under “New Need”, pick the customer and the main contact. If the customer is not on the list, choose “+ Create new customer” and type its name: it is created together with the Need. The same goes for “+ Create new contact”.

Type the subject (what they need, in one line) and the “Result the customer wants (what they want to achieve)”: with that written, the “Need” step is done. Then the request detail and, if needed, the notes for internal use: those never reach the customer.

Type the product or spare part code, or pick it from the list of those already registered (SOLU brings its description), the quantity and the customer's machine. Upload photos or files if there are any.
Leave the date of the next contact and the “We received your request” email box ticked, and click [[Crear Necesidad y revisar el correo]].

SOLU opens the email already written, with the Need's number: review the text, add more addresses under “To”, “CC (copy)” or “BCC (hidden copy)” if needed (separated by commas), tick the files to attach and click [[Enviar correo]]. To change the text with AI, type under “Rewrite with AI” how you want it (for example: shorter and ask for the nameplate photo) and click [[Reescribir con IA]], or use a quick button such as [[Más corto]] or [[Más cálido]]: the new text comes back to the box for you to review. If you do not want to write to the customer yet, click [[Guardar solo interno, sin enviar]]: the text stays as an internal note on the Need and the customer receives nothing.
Back on the board: on any card, use the drop-down list to move it to another stage. Cards in red say “No next movement”: nobody has decided what comes next.
journeys-board.expect: The Need gets its number (J-…), the email is logged and the next contact becomes its next move. A new code is registered in Find parts, and the machine stays on that customer's list, so they are not typed again. If you untick the email box, the button says “Create Need” and nothing is sent. The board hides closed Needs and those lost more than 90 days ago.

journey.why: The one workspace for a need: what is happening now, what is coming, and three dates side by side (carrier ETA, SOLU's expected date and the promise to the customer).
steps: Read the signal and its cause at the top.

Look at the path of steps and, right below it, the box “TO FINISH THE … STEP”: in red it says what is missing (“Missing: …”) and where to fill it in. Click the blue button on that line: [[Ir a llenarlo]], or the name of the action (“Prepare quote”, “Complete the quote”, “Open the quote”, “Record the PO”, “Open the PO”). SOLU takes you to the exact place, which is marked in red.
Set the next move and its date, and [[Guardar]]. Postpone with [[Mañana]] / [[3 días]] / [[1 semana]].
Review what changed since your last visit and click [[Marcar como visto]].
Use the tabs in order: Summary, Need, Locate, Source, Quote, Execute, Finance, Business File, Result.
journey.expect: SOLU's expected date is the carrier ETA plus 3 days plus 1 day. If the promise to the customer is earlier, it is flagged. Once nothing is missing in the box, the step turns green by itself and the next one appears. The first step, “Need”, only asks for the “Desired result”. In the “Purchase” and “Supplier payment” steps the box has one line per order and per payment, with its number, and it changes with every action: release, confirm with the supplier (one click), approve, record the execution and confirm the payment. When the work takes you out of the Need (to the quote, the supplier order, a payment, in other modules of the menu), the blue button “← Back to the Need” with its number stays in the bottom right corner: one click and you are back. The “×” removes it.

journey-catchup.t: What changed? and Catch me up
journey-catchup.why: Understand a Need in seconds, even if you have not seen it in days.
steps: Open ABC Foods' Need SJ-01842.
Click [[¿Qué cambió?]] to see what is new since your last visit.
Click [[Ponerme al día]] to see where it stands and what comes next.
Use [[Pregúntale a SOLU]] inside the Need for questions about that case.
journey-catchup.expect: The answers are built from the Need's data; it is not AI yet.

alcance.why: Separates what was asked, what is required, what is quoted, what is included, what is excluded and what still needs confirming, so nobody finds out at delivery that something was missing.
steps: Open the Need «Bombas dosificadoras» of Papeles del Sur (sample) and the Scope tab.
Review each line and its state.
For a line that is "to be confirmed", use the suggested message to ask the customer.
alcance.expect: Ambiguous words such as "complete" or "kit" are flagged. The quote cannot be presented while an important line is still to be confirmed.

need-source.why: Record exactly what the customer needs and where it will come from, before quoting.
steps: [[Necesidad]] tab: describe the result the customer wants and the need, and click [[Guardar necesidad]]. The customer's machine, the notes for internal use and “PHOTOS AND FILES” are right there.

[[Fuente]] tab: write where we will get it and, in the “Cost settlement” sheet, the first estimate of what it costs to bring it: product, shipping, taxes, customs, packing, bank wire and credit in our favor, in USD. The supplier's price (the “Product” row) can be in its own currency: choose it under “Currency the supplier is paid in”, type the price in that currency and SOLU brings the market rate and shows what it is in USD. Leave at 0 what you do not know yet. In the blue box, under «Eságara que quieres ganar», type the percentage you want: SOLU calculates the «Precio de venta» (total cost ÷ (1 − Eságara)). Click [[Guardar fuente]].
Note in the search log the suppliers' quotes and why you chose one.
need-source.expect: The calculated Eságara shows under the source, and the blue box shows the total cost as you type. When the quote is prepared, the sheet carries over in full and is refined there (supplier currency and where each amount comes from). If a quote is already open as a draft and you change the Eságara or a cost here, that quote does not change by itself: SOLU leaves the notice “Remember to adjust quote…” with the “Open the quote” button, and a pending task under MY DAY → Pending. Both go away by themselves once you save the costs on the quote.

quote.why: Build the solution, check the economics, define the promise and present only when it is complete.
steps: On the Need, open the [[Cotización]] tab and click [[Preparar cotización]]. SOLU brings the products and costs the Need already has.

At the top, the box “COMPLETE TO PRESENT” has on one form the only required things: the price of every product, the product's cost and the lead time. Fill in the red fields (the “i” next to each name explains what to write) and click [[Guardar lo que llené]]. The rest is under “Optional” and does not stop you.
Under “PRODUCTS ON THE DOCUMENT”, check each line and give it a price with “Edit”. To add another, open [[Agregar producto]] and click [[Agregar]].

Under “ECONOMICS”, fill in the “Cost settlement” sheet. In the blue box, under «Eságara que quieres ganar», type the percentage you want: SOLU calculates the «Precio de venta». Click [[Guardar costos]]: the price is put on the products. Below you see the Eságara before and after the cost of financing the payment terms.
Optional: offer alternatives with [[+ Escenario]] and [[Agregar escenario]], and mark one with [[Recomendar este]].

In the right column, “READY TO PRESENT” shows each point with “✓”, “!” (required and missing) or “·” (optional, not filled). Each point is a link: click it and SOLU takes you to where it is filled in, with the form open.

Check the document with [[Ver PDF]] (at the top), in English or Spanish. The “Price includes” row names what the price covers (product, shipping, duties and taxes, customs, packing) from the costs that have an amount on the sheet; the customer sees no cost amounts and no Eságara.
Once nothing required is missing, the box at the top turns green: click [[Presentar al cliente]] (right column, under the list). Prices become fixed.
quote.expect: After presenting it, changes need [[Crear revisión]] (Rev. 1, same number). The quote moves to “Quotes presented”. If you did not write the promise, SOLU builds it from the lead time.

liquidacion-costos.why: Before setting the price, work out everything it costs to bring the product: product, shipping, taxes, customs, packing, bank wire and credit in our favor. It is one calculation for the whole quote, and the Eságara comes from it.
steps: Open the draft quote and go down to the ECONOMICS block. The “Cost settlement” sheet is right there: nothing to open. Each cost has its row, with the amount in the middle and, on the right, where it comes from. Leave at 0 what does not apply.

“Product” row: type what the supplier charges and where it comes from (proforma, email). Right below, under “Currency the supplier is paid in”, pick the currency from the list. If it is not dollars, SOLU brings the market rate and shows how much it is in USD.

“Shipping” row: type the cost of transport to the customer in USD and where it comes from (DHL's or the carrier's quote). In the “Transit days” row type how many days the goods travel; it is not a cost.

“Taxes”, “Customs”, “Packaging”, “Bank wire” and “Other” rows: type each amount in USD. “Bank wire” is what the bank charges to send the money, not the amount sent. On the right there is a single box to say where these five amounts come from.
“Credit in our favor” row: if there is a balance in our favor with the supplier or the carrier, type the amount and where it comes from (credit note, balance). It is subtracted from the cost.

Look at the blue box under the rows: “Total cost” is calculated by itself. Under «Eságara que quieres ganar» type the percentage you want (for example 30) and adjust it as many times as needed: «Precio de venta» changes as you type, with the calculation under it (total cost ÷ (1 − Eságara)). If you leave that box empty, the price is the one the products already have. On save, SOLU puts that price on the products; if there are several, it splits it in the same proportion as their prices. If a cost is lower than the saved one, the «¿Por qué bajó el costo?» box appears: write the reason (for example, new proforma).
Click [[Guardar costos]].
liquidacion-costos.expect: At the top, “Current expected economics” shows the recalculated Eságara in $ and %. Under the sheet, “Customer payment habits” shows the agreed terms, in how many days the customer usually pays and what financing those days costs: SOLU brings it by itself. If you typed a credit in our favor without saying where it comes from, or a cost went down and you did not write the reason, SOLU saves nothing and asks you for it. The sheet can only be edited while the quote is a draft; after presenting it, changes are made with “Create revision”.

solucion.why: Explains to the customer why this solution solves their need, using only value attributes that have evidence in this case.
steps: Open the Need's Solution tab.
Choose the value attributes that apply and their evidence.
Open the printable proposal and review it.
solucion.expect: An attribute without evidence cannot be claimed in the proposal.

esagara-exc.why: A quote with Eságara under 20% is not presented without an approved exception.
steps: On a quote under 20%, request the exception and write the reasons.
The Commercial Director or Management reviews it on this tab, with the customer's credit and payment context.
Approve or reject with a note.
esagara-exc.expect: Whoever requests the exception can never approve it. The tab shows the 90-day pattern per customer.

futuro.why: All the presented quotes waiting for a customer decision, grouped by what is needed.
steps: Open the tab and review each zone.
If you are waiting for the customer on purpose, open the quote and record it with [[Guardar espera]] and a date.
When the PO arrives, record it on the quote with [[Registrar y comparar]].
futuro.expect: A quote in a deliberate wait shows "No action today" instead of nagging you.

seguimientos.t: Follow-ups: several pending items of one customer in a single email
seguimientos.why: Follow up several requests, quotes, purchase orders, deliveries, invoices to collect and projects of the same customer with one email, instead of writing one for each item.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]] and click [[Seguimientos]]. You also get there from “Quotes presented”, with the “Follow-ups” button at the top right.
Under “1 · CUSTOMER AND PERSON”, click the customer. The number on the right is how many pending items it has. Then click the person, or leave “The whole company”.

Under “3 · PENDING WITH…” you see their open requests, quotes without a decision, purchase orders not delivered, deliveries in progress, receivables to collect and open projects. Tick the box of each item that goes in the email (up to 12).
If you want, write in the box on the right of each item what you need from the customer (for example: we still need the logo). It goes in the email, next to that point.
Click [[Generar correo de seguimiento]]. “Follow-up email” opens, already written with every item you ticked. Nothing is sent yet.

Check “To”, pick the subject and change the text if needed. Under “IF THEY DON'T REPLY” leave the box “Remind me in MY DAY → To-dos on” ticked with its date (it comes set three working days ahead), or untick it.
Click [[Enviar correo]].
seguimientos.expect: The email goes out from the company account and you return to the list with the notice “Follow-up sent…”. If you left the reminder, that day you have a to-do in MY DAY → To-dos to check whether they replied. Each item that was in the email shows “Last follow-up” with today's date, and the email is logged on the customer. Under “All customers” there are no tick boxes: to send an email you go into a customer. A project appears here when it is linked to a customer; if it does not come from a Need with a person, it reads “no person assigned” and shows for every person of that company. If you tick nothing, SOLU says: “Tick at least one pending item to generate the email”.

seguimientos-criterio.t: Follow-ups: review by urgency, days overdue or Eságara value
seguimientos-criterio.why: Review your pending items in the order that helps you: the most overdue, the most urgent or what leaves the most Eságara, for one customer or for all of them.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]] and click [[Seguimientos]]. It opens on “All customers”; to review just one, click its name under “1 · CUSTOMER AND PERSON”.
Under “2 · CRITERION”, on the “Show” row, choose what to review: “Everything”, “Requests”, “Quotes”, “Purchase orders”, “Deliveries”, “Receivables” or “Projects”.
On the “Order” row, choose “Most overdue first”, “By urgency”, “Highest Eságara first” or “Lowest Eságara first”.

To mark the urgency of an item, use the list that reads “Urgency: not marked” on its row and choose high, medium or low. It saves by itself. The same list is on the Need's page, at the top, next to the customer's name.
On the “Urgency” row, choose “High”, “Medium”, “Low” or “Not marked” to see only those.
Under “All customers”, click the customer's name, above each row, to go into that customer with the same criterion and prepare their email.
seguimientos-criterio.expect: Urgency is marked once per Need and applies to its request, its quote, its purchase order, its delivery and its invoice. Days overdue are the days since the date that counts: the quote's validity, the invoice's due date, the date required on the purchase order, the delivery date, or the request's next move. Whatever has no date or no calculated Eságara goes last. A project uses its own priority and has no Eságara. If nothing matches, SOLU says “Nothing matches this criterion” and offers “Clear the filters”.

po.why: Spots differences between what the customer ordered and what we quoted, before we commit.
steps: On the presented quote, open [[Llegó la PO · registrarla]], type the PO number and click [[Registrar y comparar]].
Review the comparison: each line, price, quantity, terms and validity.

If the date cannot be met, pick a way out under “OPTIONS TO RESOLVE THE DATE” with [[Elegir esta opción]] and record the customer's confirmation with [[Registrar confirmación]]. For the other differences (price, quantity, incoterm, payment), go down to the red box “HOW TO RESOLVE EACH DIFFERENCE”: each one states its ways out. If it was typed wrong, [[Corregir la OC]]; if the company accepts it, write why and click [[Aceptar esta diferencia]].
In the right column, each precondition of “ACCEPT PO” is a link that takes you to where it is resolved. Once all show “✓”, click [[Aceptar PO]].
po.expect: Accept PO stays disabled while an important difference is open or a precondition shows “!”. If the customer is new and has no credit limit, request it right there with “Request a credit review”: Finance or Management decide. Once accepted, the record cannot be edited. The PO can only be recorded on a quote presented in SOLU: if the Need was marked as quoted without that document, the red box on the Need first asks for “Prepare quote” and “Present to customer”, and then shows the “Record the PO” button. If the customer has no credit limit, the red box “MISSING: THE CUSTOMER'S CREDIT LIMIT” appears on the right: Finance or Management set it there with “Save limit”; others request it with “Request a credit review”. A PO price accepted with a note becomes the sale, and SOLU checks Eságara again at that price: if it falls below the threshold, the PO cannot be accepted. The total resolves itself once the lines are resolved.

promise.why: The committed delivery date, and an honest record when it changes.
steps: Set the date and click [[Guardar promesa]].
If you change it later, choose the cause (supplier, logistics, customer, etc.).
promise.expect: Insights shows the original date, the revised one and the real one, and why it changed.

resultado.why: Confirm the customer really got the result they needed. If not, recover it.
steps: Record what the customer confirmed with [[Confirmar resultado del cliente]] or [[Agregar evidencia]].
If something went wrong, choose the cause and click [[Abrir Recovery]]. Pick an option with [[Elegir]].
Finish it under [[Resolver Recovery]]: successful, not recovered or no longer applies.
When the CLOSURE READINESS list is complete, close with [[Cerrar Necesidad]]. Note any signal of a future need (continuity), with a follow-up date.
resultado.expect: A continuity signal creates a follow-up task. It does not create a sales opportunity by itself.

dinero.why: All the blocked money, in four buckets, with the cause and who resolves it.
steps: Open [[Por entregar, facturar y cobrar]] and pick a case.
Read the block, which step the invoice is at and the payment promises.
Make the move that applies, or request credit if needed.
dinero.expect: Requesting credit does not approve it: Finance or Management decide.

fugas.why: Where money is delayed, by stage and by cause.
steps: Open [[Demoras del dinero]].
Look at the stage with the most days of delay.
Review the Needs behind that delay.
fugas.expect: The rules it is measured with are written on the screen.

valor.why: The catalogue of what we can claim in a proposal.
steps: Open the tab and choose an attribute.
See what evidence backs it.
valor.expect: In a proposal it is only used with evidence from that case.

foco.why: Top 5 by Eságara, decisions of the month, deals to protect, money to move and the big ones that have been still for days.
steps: Open [[Negocios de alto valor]].
Go through the Top 5 and open one.
Review the big ones that have been still for days and set a move.
foco.expect: Each row leads to its Need.

visitas.why: Prepare and close customer visits without typing what SOLU already knows.
steps: Open [[Visitas]] and click [[Planear visita]] for ABC Foods.
Review the automatic summary: open needs, quotes waiting, receivables, commitments and earlier visits.
After the visit, close it with the commitments, photos and PDF. You can dictate the notes by voice.
Review the trip's mission and budget.
visitas.expect: The AI notes draft is off until there is a key. The trip's money (budget, advance, expenses and settlement) is explained in Administration → Trips.

linea-comunicaciones.why: Each company by the last time we spoke, so no customer goes months without hearing from us.
steps: Open [[Último contacto por cliente]]. Each range says how many companies have gone that long without contact; the further right, the longer.
Open a range and pick a company.
Choose what to record: [[Llamada]], [[Videollamada]], [[Visita]], [[Correo]] or [[Nota]].
Tick the box that says how it went (for example “Answered” or “Unanswered”), write the notes and save with [[Registrar llamada]].
Management or Direction: at the bottom, change the cut-offs in months and click [[Guardar rangos]].
linea-comunicaciones.expect: An answered call, a video call or visit that took place and an email move the company to “up to date”. A note, an unanswered call or a visit being organised stay in the history, but the company stays in its range. From the company you can open its profile and diary.

perfiles.why: What hurts each customer, what they struggle with and how each person lives it at work, written after every conversation, to present our service as the solution to that struggle.
steps: Open [[Diario de clientes]] and pick a customer. At the top you see what hurts them, what they struggle with and the next follow-up.
Click [[Escribir en el diario]]. Choose which conversation it comes from: a call, video call or visit already recorded, a new one, or none if it is just a note.
Write the pain, the struggle, the impact and the personal side. The rest is under [[Presupuesto, decisión y acuerdo]].
Under “Follow-up plan”, write what you will do and when. Save with [[Guardar en el diario]].
Under People, use [[+ Anotar algo de esta persona]]: what they want to achieve, what complicates their day, what worries them, how they decide. Always with how we know it.
At the bottom, keep what is handy to have with [[+ Agregar documento]], [[+ Agregar producto]] or [[+ Agregar marca]]: a photo or PDF, a link, or both.
perfiles.expect: The follow-up becomes a to-do of yours with its date in MY DAY → To-dos. A new call, video call or visit also goes into the customer's history and counts in “Last contact per customer”. What is noted about a person is about their work: SOLU does not store health, religion, politics or family-life data, or labels, and explains why. Only the commercial team sees that part; Finance and Administration see the diary.

metas.why: Five goals a month, measured with what happened in SOLU.
steps: Open [[Mis metas]].
Look at the pace you need to get there.
Read “Where the path narrows”.
metas.expect: Only you and management see them. There is no team ranking.

recetario.t: Monthly recipe: from your sales goal to your daily activities
recetario.why: Know how many deals, quotes, first meetings, pitches to decision makers and prospecting activities you need this month, and per day, to reach your sales goal.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]] and click [[Mis metas]]. At the top is the “MONTHLY RECIPE” block with your name.

Type your “Sales goal for the month (USD)” and “Your average sale (USD)”. If SOLU already knows your real average sale over the last 12 months, it shows it below the boxes: click “Use this value” to take it.

Check the four ratios: out of how many quotes you close 1, out of how many first meetings 1 quote comes, out of how many decision makers who hear your pitch 1 first meeting comes, and out of how many prospecting activities you reach 1 decision maker. They start at 2, 2, 3 and 3: change them to yours.
Look at the chart: it changes as you type. It goes down from the sales goal to the “Daily prospecting activities”, using the month's working days.
Click [[Guardar mi recetario]].
recetario.expect: SOLU confirms “Recipe saved.” To the right of each bar, “So far” shows what already happened this month as recorded in SOLU, and on the last bar “Today” counts today's activities; “How «so far» is counted”, below the chart, explains each figure. Each month has its own recipe; a month already closed doesn't change. Management and the Commercial Director can view and write another person's recipe by picking them under “Person”. Management, Administration and the Commercial Director also write it in EQUIPO → Mi equipo → Organizar metas del equipo.

tabla-bateo.t: Batting table: your requests, quotes and purchase orders against your goal and your earlier months
tabla-bateo.why: See how you are doing this month in requests, quotes, purchase orders and Eságara against your goal, your averages and your best mark, what percentage you convert and how fast you respond; and see the same for a single company.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]] and click [[Mis metas]]. Below the recipe is the “BATTING TABLE” block with your name.

Read each row: “Month goal”, “Previous month”, “3-month average”, “6-month average”, “12-month average”, “My best mark”, “This month”, “Change” and “Achievement”. “My best mark” is your best earlier month, with its date. Under the “This month” figure is the month's “Projection” if the pace holds, and “Change” compares it with your 12-month average. On the right, the chart “Last 12 months and this one” shows this month in dark and the month goal as a dashed line.

To type your goals, go down to the boxes, from “# Requests goal for the month” to “Goal Quote → PO (days)”, and click [[Guardar metas de la tabla]]. For the times you type the maximum: less is better.

To see a single company: at the top of the page, next to the month, choose the company in the “Company” list and click [[Ver empresa]]. SOLU goes down to the table, now with that company only. If the company is not in the list, type its name in “Search company”, inside the block, and click “Search”.
To go back to your whole table, choose “All companies” in the same list, or click “See all companies”.
tabla-bateo.expect: SOLU confirms “Batting table goals saved.” “Achievement” shows the percentage of the goal, and “New best mark” appears when this month beats your best month. The goal of “$ Eságara” is the “Eságara won” set by Management or the Commercial Director. “Your batting” has seven percentages measured by origin group (Request → Quote, Quote → PO, Request → PO, by value, by Eságara, repurchase and reactivation), with their cases beside them, this month and in 12 months. “Batting quality” shows the average ticket, the Eságara per purchase order, the margin and the average value and Eságara per quote. “Consistency” shows the last three months with their arrow and how many months in a row you are above your average and meeting the goal. “Your speed” shows how long each step takes this month and on a 12-month average, and says “Within the goal” or “Above the goal”. With a company chosen, “Only” and its name appear, the “Month goal” and “Achievement” columns and the goal boxes are hidden, and a link leads to “Company statistics”. If you leave the quotes and purchase-order goals empty, SOLU uses those of your recipe for the month and says so with “from your recipe”. “How the batting table is counted” explains each figure. A month already closed doesn't change. Management and the Commercial Director can view and write another person's table by picking them under “Person”.

marcador.t: My scoreboard: result, batting, production, speed and coverage, with SOLU's diagnosis
marcador.why: See at a glance how you are doing against yourself and where to work: not just “you are at 82 %”, but why.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]] and click [[Mis metas]]. Below the recipe is “MY SCOREBOARD” with your name; the button “My scoreboard ↓”, next to the month, goes straight down.

Read the five boxes: “RESULT” (sales and Eságara against the goal), “BATTING” (Quote → PO this month, your 12-month personal average and your best ever), “PRODUCTION” (requests and quotes), “SPEED” (time to quote against your average) and “COVERAGE”.

Read “SOLU diagnosis”: each line says what kind of problem you have this month (batting, volume of opportunities, economic quality or sustainability) and what to work on. “Work here” marks the most important.
Under “Required pace” see how much you need to produce per working day in purchase orders and in Eságara to meet the goal.

Under “Goal coverage” compare what is missing of your sales goal with your quotes presented without a decision. Under 100 % means you need to generate new opportunities; from 3X, your work is to convert them.
marcador.expect: The scoreboard is not filled in: it comes from what is recorded in SOLU and from your goals. Without goals it says “no goal” and the pace and coverage do not show: type your goals in the batting table or in “GOALS PER COMPANY”. The diagnosis, the pace and the coverage show only for the current month. They come from fixed rules, with no AI; “How the scoreboard is counted” explains them. It never compares you with another person.

metas-empresa.t: Goals per company: each customer's sales goal
metas-empresa.why: So your month's goal is not a figure handed down from above: each customer has its goal, the sum is yours and everyone's sum is the team's.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]] and click [[Mis metas]]. Click “Goals per company ↓”, next to the month, or go down to the “GOALS PER COMPANY” block.
For each company look at the “Average monthly sale (12 months)” and what it has under “Month sales”.
Choose the “Potential” (High, Medium or Low) and type each company's “Month sales goal (USD)”. Don't take it from the average alone: think history, potential, trend and strategy.
If you want, also type how many requests and quotes you expect from each company under “Month # Requests goal” and “Month # Quotes goal”; under each box, “so far” says how many it has.
On the “Others” row type the goals for everything without its own goal.
Click [[Guardar metas por empresa]].
metas-empresa.expect: SOLU confirms “Goals per company saved.” The “Total” row adds up your goals, and those sums become your “$ Purchase orders”, “# Requests” and “# Quotes” goals in the batting table (it says “sum of your goals per company”), in the scoreboard and in the coverage, unless you typed another one in the batting table's boxes. What you save stays in force the following months: the new month says “These goals come from…” until you save that month's. “Achievement” compares the month's purchase orders with each company's goal. The company's name opens the batting table for that company only. In EQUIPO → Mi equipo → Organizar metas del equipo, the “Sum of goals per company” column shows each person's and the “Team total”. A month already closed doesn't change.

desarrollo-cartera.t: Portfolio development: reactivate, deepen and open opportunities
desarrollo-cartera.why: So the month does not depend only on the requests that arrive by themselves: measure what you do so that more exist.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]], click [[Mis metas]] and go down to “PORTFOLIO DEVELOPMENT”.

Read the six rows: “Customers reactivated”, “Customers deepened”, “New contacts”, “New decision makers”, “New areas explored” and “New opportunities generated”. Under each name it says how it is counted.
Type your month's goal in the boxes below and click [[Guardar metas de desarrollo]].
desarrollo-cartera.expect: SOLU confirms “Development goals saved.” and “Achievement” shows the percentage of each goal. Only what is recorded in SOLU counts: contacts, Needs, and the plants, areas, white spaces and future opportunities of Mercado. A customer counts as reactivated when its previous Need was 180 days ago or more.

presupuesto-proponer.t: Commercial budget: propose a company's goals for the year and send them for approval
presupuesto-proponer.why: Write down, company by company, how much you expect in purchase orders and in invoicing each month of the year. SOLU proposes from the history; you adjust, explain and send to your leader.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]] and click [[Presupuesto comercial]]. At the top you choose the “Year”. The list “…'S COMPANIES” shows each company with last year's purchase orders, the projected close, Eságara, the trend and the “State” of its budget.
On the company's row click [[Presupuestar]]. If the company is not in the list, search for it below under “Add another company”.

Read “HISTORY OF…”: requests, quotes, purchase orders, Eságara and invoicing of the three years before, with the monthly average of 3, 6 and 12 months. “See the sources of these figures” opens each record with its original value, the rate applied and the value in pesos.

Under “Assumptions (simulator)” check what SOLU measured: growth, seasonality, average ticket, the batting percentages and the Eságara objective. Change what you need and click [[Aplicar la sugerencia de SOLU a los 12 meses]] to recalculate the months. The history is not touched.

Under “Proposal… · January to December” type or correct “PO goal ($ M)” and “Invoicing goal ($ M)” for each month, in millions of pesos. The rows below show what the goal takes: “# POs objective”, “Eságara objective”, “Quotes required” and “# Requests required”.
Choose the “Company's potential”, write the “ECSA strategy for this company” and, if your figures are not SOLU's suggestion, the “Justification”.
Click [[Guardar borrador]] to continue later, or [[Enviar a aprobación]] when it is ready.
presupuesto-proponer.expect: SOLU confirms “Draft saved.” or “Proposal sent for approval.” and the state goes from “Not started” to “Draft” and to “Submitted”. Purchase orders and invoicing are two separate budgets: one is not copied from the other. “Annual” is always the sum of the twelve months. Where SOLU has too few cases it says “not enough basis” and asks you to type the figure. If the “Justification” is missing, SOLU says so, marks the box in red and keeps the draft saved. A submitted proposal doesn't change: “Withdraw the submission” makes it a draft again. The line “Reactivations and prospects” is for what you expect to sell to companies without their own budget: it has no history and no suggestion. Management and the Commercial Director can write another person's proposal by choosing them under “Negotiator”.

presupuesto-aprobar.t: Commercial budget: approve or return the proposal of someone on your team, and correct an approved budget
presupuesto-aprobar.why: So every budget is reviewed by the person's leader, with who, when and why; and what is approved never changes without a trace.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]], click [[Presupuesto comercial]] and then [[Aprobaciones]]. “WAITING FOR YOUR DECISION” lists the proposals sent to you. They also show in TEAM → Pending approvals.
Click “Open and decide”. Review the history, the assumptions, the twelve months and the negotiator's “Justification”.
Go down to “APPROVAL AND TRAIL”. If you agree, click [[Aprobar presupuesto]]. If something must change, write “What must be reviewed” and click [[Devolver al negociador]].
To correct a budget already approved, its negotiator writes the “Reason for the new version” and clicks [[Abrir versión nueva]]: a draft opens with the same figures and goes through approval again.
presupuesto-aprobar.expect: SOLU confirms “Budget approved. It is locked: a change needs a new version.” or “Proposal returned to the negotiator with your reason.” Only the person's assigned leader approves; if they have none, Management or the Commercial Director. Nobody approves their own proposal. The “Versions” table keeps each version with its totals, and “What happened to version…” shows who did what and when, with the figures before and after. The approved version stays official until the new one is approved. The state becomes “In force” when Management or the Commercial Director publish the year's budget.

presupuesto-consolidacion.t: Commercial budget: see the sum by negotiator, team and company, and the gap against the company objective
presupuesto-consolidacion.why: See how much the goals of all companies add up to and how much is missing for the company objective, without anyone inflating goals silently.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]], click [[Presupuesto comercial]] and then [[Consolidación]].
At the top choose “Latest proposal” (everything written, in any state) or “Approved only”.
Read “COMPANY → TEAM → NEGOTIATOR → CUSTOMER”: each row is the exact sum of the ones beneath it, with “Annual POs”, “Invoicing”, “Eságara”, “Margin” and “State”.
Under “TWELVE MONTHS” choose the indicator to see January to December; “Show the companies too” opens the detail per company.
Management or the Commercial Director write the year's objective under “COMPANY OBJECTIVE AND GAP” and click [[Guardar objetivo]]. The column “Gap to assign” shows what is missing.
Review “CHECKS BEFORE TRUSTING THE SUM” and, once the proposals are approved, publish the year under “PUBLISH THE BUDGET”.
presupuesto-consolidacion.expect: SOLU confirms “Company objective saved.” The objective changes nobody's goal: it only shows the gap to review and assign. “Margin” is worked out from the totals (total Eságara over total POs), never as an average of percentages. A company budgeted by two negotiators is added only once, each with their part. On publishing, the approved budgets become “In force”. [[Exportar a CSV]] downloads the consolidation (Management, Commercial Director and Finance). A negotiator sees only their budget; a leader, theirs and their team's.

presupuesto-cumplimiento.t: Commercial budget: compare real with budget and attend to the radar
presupuesto-cumplimiento.why: Know how each company is doing against what was budgeted as of today, and which customers need attention before it is late.
steps: Open [[COMERCIAL]], click [[Presupuesto comercial]] and then [[Cumplimiento y radar]]. Choose the “Year”.
Read the boxes at the top: achievement of “PURCHASE ORDERS” and “INVOICING”, “PACE TO DELIVER” per working day and “IF THE CURRENT PACE HOLDS”.
Under “REAL AGAINST BUDGET” compare, by negotiator and company, “POs expected by today” with “Real POs”, the “PO achievement”, the “Shortfall today” and the same for invoicing.
Go down to “RADAR”. Each detection shows the fact, its figures and the “Next action”. Adjust the to-do's text and date and click [[Asignar pendiente]].
presupuesto-cumplimiento.expect: SOLU confirms “To-do created for the negotiator. They see it in MY DAY → To-dos.” The month in course is compared by working days gone, not against the full month. It compares with the approved budget; where there is none yet, with the latest proposal. A purchase order counts when it is accepted; a rejected one does not. “Real without a budget” lists what was sold to companies nobody budgeted. The radar uses fixed rules, no artificial intelligence: it shows the fall or the change with its figures, never states the cause. “How the radar detects” explains each rule. Before the year starts, achievement says it has not started and the radar already works.

cobertura.why: When you are away, another person looks after your Needs for a while.
steps: Open [[Cobertura]].
Choose who covers you, the dates and, if it is not everything, what the coverage is for.
Review the handover: each pending item says whether it must move, whether a customer decision is likely, whether it is waiting, whether it can wait or whether it is protected.
When you return, open the coverage: read what happened and click [[Ya lo leí: recibir mi trabajo de vuelta]].
cobertura.expect: The coverage ends by itself on the end date. It never delegates approvals. You remain responsible for your Needs: when you return, the only things that come back are the open to-dos in the name of whoever covered you.

mejora.why: Your own funnel of the last 90 days against the 270 before, in plain words.
steps: Open [[Mi mejora]].
Read where you improved and where most deals were lost.
Read the suggestions.
mejora.expect: It does not compare you with the team.

cierres.why: Daily, weekly and monthly close: what happened, what we learned, the visible future and the next moves.
steps: Open [[Resumen del día, semana y mes]].
Choose day, week or month.
Review the next moves.
cierres.expect: Everything comes from what happened in SOLU; there is no report to write.

despacho.why: After accepting the customer's PO, it says exactly what to dispatch, where to and with which documents.
steps: Accept a PO with [[Aceptar PO]].
Open Dispatch on the Need. The destination, who receives and the customer promise come prefilled from the PO, the quote and the customer: check them.
Click [[Emitir a Operaciones]].
despacho.expect: It comes from the accepted commitment (the frozen PO), not from the editable quote. Without the instruction the delivery cannot leave: that is why, when the Need reaches the delivery step, the red box asks for it first, with the button “Issue the instruction” that leads straight to the form. If it must change later, a new version is issued with the reason.

compras.why: Buy exactly what was quoted, keep versions and schedule the supplier payments.
steps: On the Need's [[Ejecución]] tab, pick from the “Which supplier do we buy from?” list (SOLU suggests one by name: confirm it) and click [[Preparar Supplier PO desde la cotización]]. If the supplier is not in the list, click [[+ Crear proveedor nuevo]]: saving it brings you back here with it already picked.
SOLU opens the order. Review it and save the changes with [[Guardar borrador]].

In the right column, RELEASE READINESS shows each point with “✓” or “!”. Each point is a link: click it and SOLU takes you to where it is resolved. Once nothing is open, click [[Liberar Supplier PO]].
Under PAYMENT PLAN, click [[Solicitar este pago]] on each milestone. If the order must change later: [[Crear nueva versión]].
compras.expect: Payment requests go to Administration → Supplier payments for verification. If the list says “Missing: request the authorization of this purchase” (for example, a first purchase from a new supplier), click that line and request it on the requirement. If it says “Missing: this purchase must be authorized”, the list names who can do it: that person signs in, opens the link and clicks “Approve”. Whoever requests it does not authorize it, except Management: if Management requested it, it can authorize it itself and the record says so. If a Need was left with one draft order too many (a duplicate), open it and, under the release button, use “Discard this draft”: while it exists, the “Purchase” step waits for it. Preparing the same order again no longer creates a duplicate: SOLU opens the existing one.

logistica.why: The goods coming from the supplier: where they are, when they will really arrive and whether the customer's result is at risk.
steps: Open a shipment. Update the date under [[Nueva ETA del transportista]].
If customs holds it: [[Retenido en aduana]], and then [[✓ Liberado por la aduana]] when it is released.
On arrival: [[El transportista entregó]]. If something does not match: [[Registrar discrepancia]].
logistica.expect: If the shipment arrives at our warehouse, it is received on the supplier order (RECEIVING block) and the shipment is marked received by itself; delivery to the customer comes later, from “Customer deliveries”. If it goes straight to the customer, confirming their receipt creates the delivery note. The Need's dates are updated from the shipment.

sin-despachar.why: Every accepted order that has not left yet, with the reason and who has the next step.
steps: Read the cause on each row (no supplier purchase, source not confirmed, in transit…).
Click the button to open the Need and resolve what is missing.
sin-despachar.expect: What is late shows as urgent. Rows in transit show the estimated arrival date, or say there is no carrier date yet.

remisiones.why: The proof of what was delivered, the basis for invoicing.
steps: Click [[Nueva remisión]], fill it in and click [[Registrar remisión]].
From the delivery note, click [[Emitir factura]] when it is ready.
remisiones.expect: The delivery note shows in the Need's File.

por-facturar.why: Money we already earned but have not invoiced yet.
steps: Review the list.
Click [[Emitir factura]] on each one that is ready.

ops-inicio.why: What needs attention first, what is ready for the next step, promises at risk and healthy waits. Order volume is never the headline.
steps: Open [[Inicio]] in Operations.
Read “Needs attention” first and open a row.
Review “READY FOR NEXT STEP”: each row leads to the screen where it is done.
ops-inicio.expect: Each row says what is missing and which Need it belongs to. What is going well shows as a wait, with no alarm.

ops-altovalor.why: Every accepted Need with Eságara of USD 2,000 or more, visible until everything is delivered and collected.
steps: Open [[Alto valor]].
Read a card: promise, what is at stake, money already committed, next milestone and risks.
Click the code to open the Need.
ops-altovalor.expect: Those with risk come first. “No known risk” means SOLU sees nothing material with what is recorded.

ops-requerimientos.why: Before buying: what is needed, for which Need or for stock, and whether the purchase needs approval.
steps: Open [[Requerimientos]] and click a requirement. At the top, “CAN IT BE PURCHASED?” says what is missing, who it affects and how it is resolved.
If the purchase needs authorization, go down to “PURCHASE AUTHORIZATION”, write the reason and click [[Pedir autorización]].
Whoever authorizes decides right there with [[Autorizar]], [[Devolver con pregunta]] or [[No autorizar]]. If it is above their limit: [[Escalar a Gerencia]].
When nothing is missing, click [[Crear la orden al proveedor]].
ops-requerimientos.expect: Whoever requests cannot authorize their own purchase. Without authorization the supplier order cannot be created. A routine purchase does not need it. The limit and who authorizes are at the end of the list, under “Purchase authorization policy”. To buy for stock without a Need, use “+ Stock purchase” on the list.

ops-negociacion.why: What the supplier confirmed versus what we ordered, and the real savings with their evidence.
steps: On an order, record the supplier's first quote.

When the supplier accepts the order, in the SUPPLIER CONFIRMATION block click [[El proveedor confirmó la orden tal cual]]: it is sent and confirmed in one click. If they changed price, quantity, date or terms, open the form in that block: SOLU compares and shows the differences.

If you got a better price, go down to the SAVINGS block, open “+ Record saving” and answer the five questions in order: kind of saving, what we were going to pay, what we finally paid, how much was passed on to the customer, and the proof. SOLU works out the saving while you type. Click [[Registrar ahorro]].
ops-negociacion.expect: The “Record saving” button only turns on when there is a saving (what was paid is less than planned), and it is saved with its proof. For a supplier saving, “what we were going to pay” is always their first quote. Recording savings is optional: it is not needed to release the order. Differences between what was ordered and what was confirmed stay in view until resolved.

ops-compromisos.why: The milestones the supplier promised (ready, production, pickup), each with its date and its evidence.
steps: Open the order and go down to the “WHAT THE SUPPLIER PROMISED” block. If it is empty, choose the order type and click [[Crear hitos]]: the milestones change depending on whether it is stock, made to order, a service or a repair.
On each milestone, type the date the supplier gave and where it came from, and click [[Guardar]].
When it happens, mark it with [[Ocurrió]] and the evidence.
ops-compromisos.expect: Before its date it is a healthy wait. Once the grace days pass without evidence, it shows under attention.

ops-flete.t: Freight: what to move and with whom
ops-flete.why: Weight, dimensions and packages before asking for transport, and the comparison of the freight options.
steps: Open the order and go down to the “Freight” block. Open [[Preparar el flete]] (if it was already prepared it is called [[Datos para el transporte]]; it comes filled with what SOLU already knows), complete pickup, weight, dimensions and packages, and click [[Guardar datos del flete]].

Look at the block's label: “N items missing: see which ↓” or “Ready to book transport”. Below, the red box names each missing item (“Missing: Commercial invoice”…) and what to do. Click [[Ir a llenarlo]]: the form opens on that field, marked in red. Fill it in and save again.
For each transport quote you receive, open [[+ Agregar opción de transporte]], fill it in and click [[Agregar opción]].
Choose one with [[Elegir]]. If it is not the cheapest, SOLU asks for the reason.
ops-flete.expect: To book transport only five items are required: pickup address, destination, ready date, number of packages and gross weight. The rest (contact, hours, dimensions, packaging, documents) is optional. The chosen option stays as the baseline to check the carrier's invoice later.

ops-recepcion.why: On receipt we check it is the right product, in good condition, complete and with documents; not just the quantity.
steps: Choose the warehouse and type the units received per line.
If something is not right, mark it and write what you saw.
Add weight, dimensions and up to 8 photos.
Click [[Registrar recepción]].
ops-recepcion.expect: What is in doubt goes to quarantine and does not count as available. An issue opens an exception in Operations.

ops-inventario.why: Physical, committed and available are three different numbers.
steps: Open [[Inventario]].
If something is “In doubt”, decide: [[Liberar: está bien]], [[Dañado]] or [[Devolver al proveedor]], always with the reason.
Review the table by warehouse and part number.
ops-inventario.expect: Units in quarantine or damaged never go out to a customer.

ops-despachos.why: The physical delivery to the customer: dispatched, delivered and ready to invoice are three different facts.
steps: On the Need, open Dispatch, click [[+ Nuevo despacho]], choose the units and [[Crear despacho]]. Open it from the list.
Record what the customer requires with [[+ Agregar requisito del cliente]] and mark it fulfilled.
Click [[Salió hacia el cliente]].
On delivery: who received it and [[Entregado: crear remisión]]. If it could not be done: [[No se pudo entregar]].
If the customer gives a goods-receipt number (MIGO or other), save it.
ops-despachos.expect: It does not leave without Commercial's instruction or with requirements pending. A failed attempt stays in the history, returns the goods to stock and the dispatch is scheduled again. If the instruction is missing, the dispatch says so and carries the link “Issue the instruction now →”.

ops-auditoria.why: Compares what the carrier charged with what was quoted, what was declared and what we measured.
steps: Click [[+ Registrar factura del transportador]] and fill in number, total and chargeable weight.
Read the result: matches, within normal, review difference or a claim is recommended.
If it applies, [[Abrir reclamo al transportador]].
When the credit note arrives, record it with [[Crédito recibido]].
ops-auditoria.expect: A "yes" from the carrier is not money recovered: it only counts with the credit note and the amount received. If there is nothing to compare against, SOLU says so.

ops-aduana.why: What is missing to import, the tariff classification with its source, expected versus actual duties, and holds.
steps: Click [[+ Abrir caso de aduana]].
Fill in classification, origin, declared value, consignee and broker.
Mark the classification as validated only if you write who validated it.
ops-aduana.expect: A classification used before is history, not validation. The "N missing to import" list goes down as you complete it.

ops-transportadores.why: The carrier accounts and the rule used to calculate each one's chargeable weight.
steps: Review the rules table: divisor, rounding, tolerance and claim threshold.
Management: [[Cambiar o agregar una regla]] with the values from the contract.
Tick «Confirmada contra el contrato» only when the rate sheet says so.
ops-transportadores.expect: A password is never typed here: credentials live in the server's settings.

ops-garantias.why: What was covered and for how long, and the cases the customer opens after delivery.
steps: On the Need, open “Warranty and claims” and click [[+ Registrar garantía]].
If the customer reports a problem: [[+ Abrir caso del cliente]].
Add notes as it progresses and close it with what was done, who was responsible and what it cost.
ops-garantias.expect: SOLU says whether it was within warranty on the day of the report. The cost of the case goes into the Need's real costs.

ops-experiencias.why: What we learned supplying a product, so the team does not rediscover it.
steps: Click [[+ Registrar experiencia]] and write the part number and what we learned.
If it could be published, write the public draft.
Management, Commercial Direction or Marketing tick the 7 confidentiality points.
ops-experiencias.expect: SOLU publishes nothing. It warns if the draft seems to carry a price, a serial number or the customer's name. If the draft changes, the review starts again.

ops-metricas.why: How the operation performed in the last 12 months, counted from what was recorded.
steps: Open [[Métricas]].
Read each figure with the number of cases it comes from.
ops-metricas.expect: With fewer than 5 cases it shows the count and not a percentage. There is no comparison between people.

ops-config.why: The thresholds SOLU uses to decide what to show as attention, and the warehouses.
steps: Change a threshold and click [[Guardar umbrales]].
Add a warehouse with [[+ Agregar bodega]].
ops-config.expect: Each change is kept as a version with who and when. A warehouse with stock cannot be deactivated.

facturacion.why: Issue an invoice only when everything the customer requires is ready.
steps: Review the BILLING REQUIREMENTS list, built from the customer's billing profile.
Add what is missing on each requirement: [[Pedir al cliente]] or [[Llegó: registrar]].
When the delivery says “Ready to Bill?”, click [[Emitir factura]]. Download the PDF.
Record its state in accounting under [[Puente contable]]: ID confirmed, sent and waiting for its ID, or we do not know whether it was created.
facturacion.expect: The invoice PDF does not carry bank details yet: the company's bank profile has not been verified.

cobrar.why: What customers owe, how much is overdue and what they promised.
steps: Review the open invoices by age.
When a customer commits to a payment date, click [[Registrar promesa]].
cobrar.expect: "Sent" or "approved" does not mean paid. An invoice is paid only after a reconciled payment.

pagos-recibidos.why: Assign the money that arrived to the right invoices.
steps: Record the payment with [[Registrar]].
Click [[Ver facturas]], apply it with [[Aplicar]] and then [[Conciliar]].
pagos-recibidos.expect: A bank receipt never marks an invoice as paid by itself. Unapplied money shows in a notice. Overpayments need a note before reconciling.

pagos-proveedores.why: Pay suppliers safely: independent verification, approval within limits and confirmed execution.
steps: Someone other than the requester checks the bank details and clicks [[Registrar verificación]].
An approver within their limit clicks [[Aprobar solicitud]].
After sending the transfer: [[Registrar ejecución]].
When the bank confirms it: [[Confirmar: el dinero salió]].
pagos-proveedores.expect: Only the last step marks it as paid. A bank-account change is a full stop until verified by phone on a known number. Never accept an account change by email or WhatsApp. Whoever requests a payment does not verify or approve it; the only exception is Management, which may do so on a payment it requested itself, and the record says so.

pagos-exterior.why: Payments to suppliers abroad, for the bank and the accountant.
steps: Choose the dates and click [[Filtrar]].
Download the CSV.
pagos-exterior.expect: The CSV opens in Excel with one row per payment.

cupos.why: How much credit each customer has, and the approved exceptions.
steps: For a customer already in the table: on its row, open “Change limit”, type the value and [[Guardar]].
For a customer not shown yet: open “Set a limit for another customer”, type the value next to its name and [[Guardar]].
When an order exceeds it, a manager can click [[Aprobar excepción]].
cupos.expect: On saving, SOLU confirms “Limit saved for…” and leaves you on that customer's row. Customers above their limit are flagged. From a customer's PO there is no need to come here: its red box “MISSING: THE CUSTOMER'S CREDIT LIMIT” has “Save limit” (Finance or Management) or “Request a credit review” (everyone else). To test SOLU by hand without credit stopping an order, Management has the “Limits for testing” block at the top: it raises to USD 1,000,000 the limit of sample and test customers (or of all). It lowers no limit.

adm-banco.t: Bank: upload the statement and explain movements
adm-banco.why: What the bank says next to what SOLU already knows. SOLU suggests; a person confirms.
steps: The first time: [[+ Registrar cuenta bancaria]] (name and last 4 digits).
Download the Bank of America movements as CSV, choose the file and click [[Subir y leer]].
On each movement: accept a suggestion with [[Sí, es este]] or use [[Decir qué es]].
Bank charges and transfers between own accounts are set aside with a note.
adm-banco.expect: Uploading the same period twice duplicates nothing. If SOLU does not recognise the columns, it loads nothing and shows the headings it saw.

adm-retenciones.why: What the customer withholds when paying: it lowers what the invoice owes, but it is not money received.
steps: Choose the customer and click [[Ver facturas]].
At the bottom, under Withholdings: [[+ Registrar retención]], with invoice, type and amount.
Add the certificate number when it arrives.
adm-retenciones.expect: The invoice balance goes down on every screen. The withholding shows in the customer's history and never in the list of payments received.

adm-esagara.why: What each Need really left: the protected Eságara versus the one expected today with the real costs, and why it changed.
steps: Open [[Eságara real]] and click a Need.
Read the three figures and the “Why it changed” table.
Add a cost that is not recorded elsewhere with [[+ Agregar un costo de esta Necesidad]].
Finance, Administration or Management mark the close: open, substantially complete or final.
adm-esagara.expect: The lines of “Why it changed” always add up to the total change. "Final" keeps that day's figures and blocks new costs until reopened.

adm-inicio.why: Only what needs someone today: cash, credit, collections, payments, budget, assets and obligations, unreconciled money, and Eságara and commissions.
steps: Open [[ADMINISTRACIÓN]]. At the top are the groups: Today, Money, Resources, Close and Setup.
Read each matter: what is happening, how much it weighs, why and what to do.
Click the action on the right to go where it is resolved.
adm-inicio.expect: What is fine shows on a single green line. People outside Administration, Finance, Direction or Management see their own: their file, their assets and their purchases.

adm-exposicion.why: Seven different exposures: cash, customers, suppliers, stock, currency, assets and contracts.
steps: Open [[Riesgo de los recursos]].
Go through the seven blocks; each has its link to the detail.
adm-exposicion.expect: There is no score or total that joins them. What is in another currency is shown apart, without converting.

adm-tesoreria.t: Treasury: from what is in the bank to what is free
adm-tesoreria.why: What the bank shows is not what can be spent. SOLU brings it down step by step and projects cash at 7, 30, 60 and 90 days.
steps: Under “ACCOUNTS AND CONFIRMED BALANCES”, type the balance, the date and where the figure comes from, and click [[Confirmar]].
Read “AVAILABLE LIQUIDITY”: banks, minus restricted, minus reserved, minus committed.
Open [[Apartar dinero]] to reserve an amount: what it is for and who decided it.
Under «Lo que SOLU no puede saber solo», add payroll, taxes or a loan instalment with [[Agregar]].
Review “PROJECTED CASH” and open “WHAT IS COMING, BY KIND” to see each movement.
adm-tesoreria.expect: A confirmed balance is not edited: a new one replaces it and the earlier one stays as history. If cash goes negative, SOLU shows the shortfall, the date and what could move today. What is contracted or delivered but not invoiced does not count as receivable.

adm-pagar.why: What must be paid today, in 7 and in 30 days, and each supplier invoice compared with its order and with what was received.
steps: Review the “PAYMENT CALENDAR”.
